topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: integration tests for kona-node safedb
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473.

## Scope

Prove the integration end to end against kona-node, not just in unit tests.

Acceptance suites:

- Remove `SkipOnKonaNode` from `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync` and run `safeheaddb_clsync` against kona-node. Closes #22265.
- Run `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` against kona-node. Closes #22279.
- Add an op-node parity check: on a network with one op-node and one kona-node verifier, `checkSafeHeadConsistent` passes with kona-node as the checked node and op-node as the source of truth, and the reverse.

Proofs stack:

- An output-root fault dispute game is played to resolution by an op-challenger whose only rollup node is kona-node.
- op-proposer in super-root mode and op-dispute-mon run against kona-node only.

Soak:

- A kona-node on a devnet runs 24 hours with the flag on and a contiguity check (safedb-scan from infrastructure-services, or an in-tree equivalent) reports no gap. Record restarts during the soak and confirm the history survives them.

## Done

- [ ] Both safeheaddb suites pass against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` passes against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] Parity test exists and passes.
- [ ] Challenger, proposer and dispute-mon tests against kona-node only exist and pass.
- [ ] Soak result is posted on #23473.

topIssues.title: op-deployer: interop and super-root games still gated by devFeatureBitmap in v0.9.0-dev-test.2
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Expectation

With the v0.9.0 contracts, interop and super-root games are part of the release. A fresh deployment should therefore not need `devFeatureBitmap` bits `0x1` (`OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP`) and `0x10000000` (`SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`) in `globalDeployOverrides`.

The `op-deployer/v0.9.0-dev-test.1` changelog also says: "devfeatures: Enable super root games migration by default (#21689)".

## Actual

All of the following is at tag `op-deployer/v0.9.0-dev-test.2`:

- `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/l2genesis.go`: `buildDevFeatureBitmap` returns `interop feature in devFeatureBitmap does not match the UseInterop intent flag` when `useInterop=true` and bit `0x1` is absent.
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol` still gates `CrossL2Inbox`, `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`, `ETHLiquidity`, `SuperchainETHBridge` and `UndeliveredMessageExporter` on `OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP` (`Predeploys.assertGates`).
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/deploy/DeployImplementations.s.sol` only deploys the `SuperFaultDisputeGame` / `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` implementations when either bit is set, and asserts they are absent otherwise.
- `OPContractsManagerV2.sol` (around line 753) reads `isDevFeatureEnabled(SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION)` to decide super-root mode in `deploy`; `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator.sol` (around line 951) does the same.

Net effect: without `0x10000000`, an interop chain cannot be deployed with `respectedGameType` 5 or 9 at genesis.

## Impact

- Devnet tooling (netchef in `devnets-private`) must keep passing both bits for every interop / super-root network.
- A user who reads "interop is included" in v0.9.0 and omits the bitmap gets a late failure at L2 genesis, after the L1 contracts have already been broadcast, or a non-interop genesis if the check is bypassed.
- Example network: devnets-private PR #2317 (`int-sr-0`).

## Ask

Either:

1. Default these two bits on (or remove the gates) in op-deployer v0.9.0, so an intent with `useInterop=true` deploys the interop predeploys and super-root games without a bitmap; or
2. Document in the v0.9.0 release notes that the bitmap remains required, and which bits.

---
Filed by Claude Code on behalf of jelias2

topIssues.title: Remove IFaultDisputeGame dependency from AnchorStateRegistry
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
The AnchorStateRegistry checks that the anchorStateRegistry() from the dispute game matches the AnchorStateRegistry itself via a cast to `IFaultDisputeGame`. This won't work for any game type that doesn't have a `anchorStateRegistry()` method.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/578622ccebb1b83210026f72fa9875097f4362ce/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/AnchorStateRegistry.sol#L199-L201

We should review if this is really necessary (we're trusting the game's `wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated()` method anyway so seems odd to not just require that the game was created via the DisputeGameFactory). If it is we need to add `anchorStateRegistry()` to the `IDisputeGame` interface and implement it in all game types.

topPRs.title: ci: add an optional RWX shadow that leaves CircleCI unchanged
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
Adds RWX as an optional shadow of the CircleCI PR workloads, without changing anything CircleCI runs. It replaces the approach of #23151, which rerouted about 66 CircleCI jobs through new evidence-collecting wrappers and edited justfiles and product code to feed them; that made CircleCI itself part of the experiment and hard to approve. Here CircleCI stays the only required CI, and RWX can be turned off or deleted without touching it.

**CircleCI is unchanged.** `git diff origin/develop -- .circleci justfile op-acceptance-tests rust/justfile packages op-deployer` is empty. Outside `.rwx/` and `ops/ci/`, the PR adds two CODEOWNERS lines (`/.rwx/` and `/ops/ci/` → cloud-security, as in #23151), the operator guide `docs/ai/rwx-shadow-ci.md`, and its index line in `AGENTS.md`.

**When RWX runs.** GitHub pushes to `develop`, and pushes to opt-in branches named `rwx/*`; plus RWX's `develop`-only cache-rebuild runs and manual `rwx run`. Contributor PRs never start a run or get an RWX status check (in #23151, `rust-e2e.yml` and `selector-upload.yml` fired on every branch push). None of the RWX checks is required.

**Cost.** Each `develop` push starts three RWX runs: `pr-gates.yml` (every shadowed PR workload, then the gate mirrors), `rust-e2e.yml` and `selector-upload.yml`. RWX may also start `develop`-only cache-rebuild runs. Teddy holds the cost figures privately; they are not published here. Pilot observation, not a measurement of this branch: on #23151's head (2216cd4069) the three runs took about 39, 19 and 2.5 minutes wall clock.

**Turning it off.** Set the `if:` of the three `on.github.push` triggers (`pr-gates.yml`, `rust-e2e.yml`, `selector-upload.yml`) to `false` and merge; or, immediately, a GitHub org owner suspends the RWX GitHub App or removes this repository from it. Deleting `.rwx/`, `ops/ci/`, the guide and the two CODEOWNERS lines removes it completely.

**Product-code hooks.** None remain. RWX now calls the unchanged recipes and scripts that CircleCI calls, or does the work in its own wrapper:

| #23151 hook | RWX here |
| --- | --- |
| `OP_DEPLOYER_TEST_BINARY` in `cli_runner_test.go` | The CLI test's `TestMain` builds op-deployer at verdict time, as on CircleCI: a cold build (about 35 s locally) on the four verdict workers that run the CLI groups, off the critical path |
| Runtime `CARGO_BIN_EXE_lokahi` lookup in `rust/lokahi/tests/cli.rs` | The unit-test worker extracts the nextest archive at the producer's target path, so the compile-time path resolves |
| Coverage replay in `go-ffi/trie*.go` | RWX runs coverage unseeded, like CircleCI |
| `vm.skip` reasons and the `DisputeGameFactory` fork fix in Solidity tests | Not needed: RWX runs the same fork configuration as CircleCI |
| Root `justfile`: Go runner and `_nut-prefork-state-for` reroutes | RWX runs its own Go runner over `just list-test-packages`, and the unchanged `just _check-nut-prefork-states` |
| `op-acceptance-tests/justfile` sharding and reports | The unchanged recipe; RWX answers its `circleci tests split` call with RWX's own shard plan |
| `rust/justfile` `print_commands` | The unchanged `hack` / `hack-tests-default` recipes, as CircleCI calls them |
| `nut-provenance-verify` reports, `test-interop-deposits-diff.sh` and `make-summary-deployment.sh` capture | The commands' exit status and logs |
| `ops/check-changed`, `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` | Not needed: RWX does not call `check-changed`, its routing ignores `.ci/`, and no Docker build copies `.ci/` |
| `fetch-witness-tar.sh` retry | Owned by #23772; RWX inherits it when that lands |
| `generate-flaky-tests-report.sh` anonymous API access | The only one RWX cannot avoid, so this PR drops the flaky-report shadow instead. Restoring it needs that script change (acceptance-test owners) or a CircleCI API token in an RWX vault |

**What changed relative to #23151.** The first commit imports `.rwx/` and `ops/ci/` verbatim from 2216cd4069, so the later commits show every change.
- RWX selects workloads by running CircleCI's own routing data and policy (`.circleci/routing.yml`, `collect-params.sh`, `compute-workflow-conditions.sh`) read-only, instead of a forked copy. A change under `.rwx/` or `ops/ci/` selects every workload.
- Removed what only CircleCI used: the forked routing scripts and their decision-tree tests, the 19 parity comparers that read CircleCI wrapper evidence, CircleCI adapter tests, and orphaned contract scripts. Kept `compare-ci.py`, which compares RWX results with CircleCI's normal JUnit/Go JSON/test-metadata output, and `circle-alignment.py`, which fails when a CircleCI gate's `requires:` stops matching `pr-gates.json` (it passes against `develop`).
- Dropped the flaky-report shadow: it needs either the #23151 edit to `generate-flaky-tests-report.sh` (anonymous API access) or a CircleCI API token in an RWX vault.
- Removed every reference to `codex/rwx-ci-pilot`, including the pinned L2 fork snapshot; RWX forks OP Mainnet at `latest`, like CircleCI's PR job.
- Fixed verdicts that reported false failures: an all-skipped contract selection (now counted as executed, like `check-junit-tests-ran.sh`); passing `compile_fail` doctests and `#[should_panic]` tests in the Rust and SP1 reports; Go 1.24+ `build-output`/`build-fail` events in `ci-test-results.py`; Semgrep findings, which `--json` hid from the log, are printed again.
- Every `ops/ci` unit test runs in RWX when `ops/ci/` or `.rwx/` changes: such a change selects every workload, each workload's `helper-tests` task runs its tests, and the new `ci-unit-tests` task runs the shared ones. `test_ci_layout.py` fails when no task runs a test file.

**Trade-off.** CircleCI no longer emits the byte-level parity evidence that #23151's wrappers produced, so RWX results are compared with CircleCI's normal artifacts.

**Before `rwx/*` branches work end to end**, an RWX admin needs to grant `refs/heads/rwx/*` on the test-only `optimism-go-tests-rpc-shadow` vault. Its repository grants are `develop` and `codex/rwx-ci-pilot` today; the pilot grant can go once #23151 closes. The cache vault `optimism-op-reth-shadow` keeps its `develop`-only write grant.

**Validation.** `rwx lint --dir .rwx` reports no errors (19 warnings: `mise/install` 1.1.1 exists; this PR keeps the 1.1.0 that #23151 ran with). Locally, every `ops/ci` unit test passes (396 + 44; 41 live-toolchain fixtures skip on macOS and run inside their RWX tasks), `circle-alignment.py` passes against `develop`'s CircleCI config, and ShellCheck and shfmt are clean. No hosted RWX run has been made from this branch yet.

**Review.** A CI-config review and a code review both found that CircleCI's routing omits the flags it does not enable, which turned the RWX gates red on opt-in `rwx/*` pushes without contract or Rust changes; 3e784c8acb fixes it and the routing test now fails without the fix. Accepted without a code change, please confirm:
- `required-rust-e2e` has no alignment check: its job list in `ops/ci/runtime/rust-e2e.py` matches CircleCI today and must be kept in step by hand (documented).
- The routing adapter inherits CircleCI's fixed `/tmp/pipeline-parameters.json`. RWX tasks are isolated; only two concurrent local runs of `test_rwx_metadata.py` would collide.
- The import commit still has #23151's unconditional push triggers, so this PR must be squash-merged (the repository default) and that commit never pushed as a branch head.
- The runtime scripts keep their now-unused `--provider circleci` modes, to keep this diff close to #23151; removing them is a separate cleanup.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add mock ComplianceModule and Policy for the bridge-screener devnet
topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
# DO NOT MERGE
**Description**

Adds the devnet-only compliance mocks the bridge screener integrates against, so the
off-chain service can build against real addresses and the production interfaces before the
real contracts exist.

Nothing under `src/` or `snapshots/` changes beyond a 5-line interface rename. The mocks live
in `scripts/deploy/mocks/`, which keeps them clear of the `src/`-scoped interface-mirror,
snapshot and semver checks. No OPCM, op-deployer or dev-feature changes.

`DeployComplianceMocks.s.sol` deploys the mocks and points a live Portal's `bridgeHook` at the
module. The Portal already stores a hook and `initialize` already sets one, but `initialize`
is a `reinitializer` whose version the live proxy has consumed, and that version is
`immutable`. So the script clears the proxy's `_initialized` byte and re-runs `initialize`,
the same sequence OPCM uses in `OPContractsManagerUtils.upgrade`.

A `useMockPortal` flag decides what the Portal is left running:

- **false**: re-installs the implementation the Portal already had, reading every value passed
  back to `initialize` off the Portal first, so the call changes nothing but the hook. The only
  effect on the chain is that the module joins the Portal's unsafe-target set.
- **true**: installs `MockOptimismPortal2`, which screens deposits and withdrawals through the
  hook, so the whole flow works before #23736 and the withdrawal path land. Its storage mirrors
  the real Portal's slot for slot, with a spacer for every field it does not use, so the swap
  preserves live state and is reversible. Set it false once the real paths are in.

**Tests**

`MockPolicy`: the three screening outcomes, override precedence over the per-direction
defaults, completion vs withdrawal dispatch, clearance expiry, the clear and revoke write
path, owner gating.

`MockComplianceModule`: hook entry points gated on both the caller and still being the
Portal's hook, `Held` carrying a preimage that round-trips through `hashItem`, policy-only
verdicts, the record deleted before calling out (including a re-entering policy), the disable
switch respecting the L2 nonce cutoff.

`MockOptimismPortal2`: deposit and withdrawal screening, holds emitting no
`TransactionDeposited` / `WithdrawalFinalized`, completion on committed terms, the deposit
counter distinguishing otherwise identical deposits.

`DeployComplianceMocks`: runs against a full stack. Asserts the Portal's initialized byte is
back to 4, its configuration and `l2Sender` are unchanged, and an ordinary deposit still works.
With the mock installed, asserts it reads `SystemConfig`, `AnchorStateRegistry`, `ETHLockbox`,
the maturity delay and `l2Sender` back at the live values, which is what the storage padding
exists to guarantee. A second run is refused.

162 tests pass.

**Notes for review**

- The `expiresAt` rename in the first commit follows `flux/compliance-specs`. specs#977 landed
  upstream keeping `clearedAt`, so that one is unsettled and worth a decision.
- `ItemObserved` on the Policy is mock-only. A deposit that proceeds leaves no on-chain record
  of its item ID, since `TransactionDeposited` does not carry the deposit counter.
- The script requires the L1 ProxyAdmin owner to be the broadcaster, so a multisig PAO will not
  work with it as written.
- `scripts/deploy/mocks/README.md` is the integration contract for the screener.

**Metadata**

- Part of ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#842

topPRs.title: docs: add ZK proofs documentation
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
Adds public docs for the ZK proof system, which is replacing Cannon-based fault proofs, so operators and readers have docs before ZK proofs ship.

- New "ZK Proofs" section under How the protocol works: hub, explainer, ZK dispute game, proof system, components, security, and reference.
- Operator pages: configuring op-zk-proposer and op-challenger for ZK games, verifying a ZK absolute prestate, and migrating a chain to ZK proofs via `opcm.upgrade`.
- An op-zk-proposer component page, a ZK section in the op-dispute-mon monitoring docs, and a shared "experimental" warning snippet.

Open items, marked as TODO comments in the pages:

- Standard values for `maxChallengeDuration`, `maxProveDuration`, `challengerBond`, and the init bond.
- The op-contracts release and superchain-ops template that support the ZK game.
- The op-zk-proposer image name and tag format.
- Adding op-zk-proposer to the component reference and release notes generators.
- Local prover support. The proposer currently proves only through the Succinct Prover Network.

The spec's `ZKDisputeGameConfig` includes a `verifier` field, but the OPCM struct doesn't: OPCM supplies its own `SP1PlonkAdapter`. These docs follow the code.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/3

topPRs.title: kona-node!: deliver and retry delegated forkchoice updates
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Kona delivers delegated safe-head promotions to the execution client even when unsafe and finalized do not change. A `SYNCING` response stays pending and retries on a separate cadence using current heads, allowing imports to continue; only an acknowledged `VALID` forkchoice suppresses an identical request.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23676. Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/545; this PR targets `develop` independently of catch-up liveness and finalized monotonicity.

Validation: all 111 engine tests pass, covering unchanged-target retries, changed targets, native span batching, reset acknowledgment, and build acknowledgment. All 293 dependent service/RPC/node tests and 8 focused actual service actor tests pass, including idle recovery and retry-timer behavior. Strict engine/service Clippy across all features and targets and pinned formatting pass. Independent Rust/correctness review and review of safe-head history notifications found no remaining production blockers. Full workspace lint was not completed locally.

Combined validation with the companion fixes also passes: 124 engine tests, 293 service/RPC/node tests, strict scoped Clippy, and pinned formatting. This uses a local integration checkout; the three PRs remain independent.

BREAKING CHANGE: Downstream Rust users constructing EngineState with complete struct literals must initialize forkchoice_status, normally ForkchoiceStatus::Unsent for fresh state, or use ..EngineState::default(). Exhaustive destructuring must include the new field or ..; mark Applied only after an execution-client VALID acknowledgement.

CI: 117 checks passed. The only failing test is `TestProposerProvesBelowHeadMessageOnTablePath` in [Kona acceptance job 5772627](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5772627): the ZK proposer expected 1 log batch but observed 2, exactly matching the known flake https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23612 (also seen on unrelated PRs). `main` and `ci-gate` fail as a consequence. All Rust gates, other acceptance shards, image checks, and dependency review passed. No source change was made for this unrelated failure. A targeted rerun was not possible because this environment has no configured CircleCI credentials; this PR remains draft pending that rerun.
